If you're not in a rush to grab the latest Apple product on launch day and are willing to wait a bit, Apple's certified refurbished store has always been a solid option. Generally speaking, it takes about three months from a new product launch for the first batch of refurbished units to appear on Apple's website.

Other companies have their own options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but be aware that the standards and warranty terms they use are all different……

Apple Certified Refurbished

When buying from Apple's certified refurbished store, you can typically get around a 15% discount, and the product itself is completely identical to a brand-new one. Specifically, Apple promises all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing by Apple
  • Brand new housing, so there won't be any scuffs or scratches
  • Brand new battery, so you get the same battery life as a brand-new device
  • Comes with all original accessories and cables
  • Comes with Apple's standard one-year warranty, with coverage identical to a brand-new device
  • Also eligible for purchasing AppleCare+

Basically the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box rather than the original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed typically offers more competitive pricing, but be aware that the product condition doesn't come with the same guarantees:

  • Inspection and testing performed by the seller, not Apple
  • Used housing, so there will be scuffs and scratches (see below)
  • Used battery, only guaranteed to be at 80% or above of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be original Apple products
  • Comes with a 90-day Amazon warranty instead of Apple's one-year warranty

Regarding scuffs and scratches, Amazon offers three quality tiers:

  • Premium / Excellent: No visible wear when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: Light scratches when viewed from 12 inches away, barely noticeable to the naked eye
  • Acceptable: Scratches that are easily seen and felt

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored is more vague than Amazon about what you're getting for your money:

  • No commitment on cosmetic condition, only claims "performance and reliability like new"
  • No specifics on battery condition, only as stated above
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only get 90 days. The company doesn't clearly define what each tier actually means.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want a product that's identical to a brand-new one in both appearance and Apple warranty, then Apple's refurbished store is clearly the top choice.

However, Amazon Renewed's pricing can indeed be significantly cheaper, so if you're willing to accept the trade-offs listed above, it might be a decent deal. Especially if you follow our advice and, to save money, upgrade to an iPhone 17 Pro instead of this year's new model (just missing one cable), there are some pretty tempting deals here:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro in Cosmic Orange $1,214 (originally $1,599 new) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro in Deep Blue $1,215 (originally $1,599 new) — all-time low price
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro in Silver $1,208 (originally $1,599 new) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro in Cosmic Orange $1,164 (originally $1,299 new) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro in Deep Blue $1,170 (originally $1,299 new) — all-time low price
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro in Silver $1,171 (originally $1,299 new) — just $1 off the all-time low price

As for Walmart Restored, their promises are simply too vague for my comfort, but if you're not satisfied, you can always choose to return it.
